title: Private-mode batching & caching advisor: offline safe-apply, staged rollout, and policy enforcement
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Private/VPC/on-prem customers want the cost benefits of automated batching and KV-prefix caching recommendations, but cannot tolerate silent config changes, outbound telemetry, or anything that may break regulated traffic patterns. Current autosuggest tooling (hosted) assumes metrics shipping and live A/B checks; that model is incompatible with air-gapped or policy-constrained environments.

Goal:
Build a Private-mode 'Batching & Cache Advisor' that can run in VPC or on-prem, produce conservative recommendations, and support a safe apply workflow: local dry-run, staged canary apply, automatic rollback on regression, and strict policy enforcement (org-level allowlists/denylists and RBAC). The system must operate without cloud telemetry when required, log all changes to customer audit streams, and integrate with KMS/HSM-backed secrets.

Scope and constraints:
- Runs entirely in customer-managed control plane for Private deployments, able to function in fully air-gapped environments (no external telemetry by default).
- Produces recommendations for batching window sizes, dynamic batch caps, prefix/KV caching policies, and hinting for quantization profiles where applicable.
- Default recommendations must be safe: latency-first for latency-sensitive routes, cost-first for background/async routes; do not increase token-level tail latency beyond configured SLO.
- Safe-apply flow: 1) dry-run (simulated cost/latency delta using local traces or synthetic load), 2) staged canary (config applied to a small percentage of traffic within customer capacity), 3) monitor regression signals for KPS, p99 latency, error rate, and output-quality heuristics; 4) automatic rollback on threshold breaches, with audit log entry and operator notification.
- Offline mode must accept batched trace bundles (JSONL) for environments where live sampling is prohibited. The advisor should run analysis against those bundles and produce recommendations and simulation projections.
- Policy enforcement: organization admins can define rules (e.g., do-not-change routes matching /payments/*, or only allow cache TTL <= 30s in certain regions). Advisor must evaluate recommendations against policy and mark recommended changes as blocked or requiring explicit approval.
- Auditability: every recommendation and applied change must include an immutable audit record with who initiated the action, what was changed, pre/post configs, and a link to the dry-run simulation output. Audit records should integrate with the customer's existing audit log sink (syslog/ELK/S3) in Private deployments.
- Secrets/KMS: any keys used to sign or encrypt offline bundles, or to access local telemetry stores, must be integrated with customer KMS/HSM; advisor must not persist plaintext secrets.

Acceptance criteria:
- Advisor prototype implemented as a CLI + sidecar + operator CRD that can be deployed in Private control plane or on-prem. CLI must support --dry-run, --apply-canary=<percent>, --rollback, and --offline-bundle=<path>.
- Dry-run simulation can ingest live traces or offline bundles and emit a quantified projection: expected tokens/sec, expected locost (%), expected p95/p99 delta, and a confidence score.
- Staged canary pipeline applies changes to a user-configurable subset and automatically monitors predefined signals for 10 minutes, rolling back if thresholds are violated. Thresholds are configurable per-org and per-route.
- Policy engine evaluates each recommendation and attaches one of: approved | blocked | needs-approval. Blocked suggestions should never be applied by automation.
- All actions are auditable and emitted to the customer's configured sink with the required metadata.
- Documentation and an operator runbook exist describing dry-run interpretation, rollback triggers, and manual override steps.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Conservative defaults: for routes with unknown SLAs, prefer no-op or minimal batching to avoid latency spikes. Allow architects to opt-in to aggressive cost profiles per route.
- Offline bundle format: JSONL of request/response metadata with KV cache hit traces; must be compact and signed. We will publish schema and a small local bundler for common proxies.
- Quality checks: without user feedback, guarding against hallucination or output-quality regressions is hard. We plan to implement lightweight token-level similarity heuristics and optional labeled prompt sets that the advisor can use to detect quality regressions during canary. For high-assurance customers, require labeled prompt sets as a precondition for automated apply.
- Telemetry: by default advisor runs with no external telemetry. If a customer enables telemetry forwarding, the advisor can optionally call Redwood cluster services for cross-customer benchmarking; this must be opt-in.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal prototype and design review (2 weeks).
2) Private early-access with two pilot customers (finance and SaaS) in VPC mode (4 weeks).
3) Post-pilot hardening: offline bundle UX, policy editor UI integration in Console, and additional QA (3 weeks).
4) GA in runtime-1.20 with opt-in flag and operator runbook.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Automatic changes in private environments could degrade customer SLAs. Mitigation: Default to dry-run and require explicit admin opt-in for apply; rollouts must be small canaries with automatic rollback.
- Risk: Offline bundles may miss distributional shifts. Mitigation: advise customers on sampling strategy and require periodic re-run of bundles.
